title: The rule of five
description:
Write a class from a blank page with all five special member functions.

`Image` owns a heap array of `width × height` bytes (`unsigned char`), all starting at 0.

- `Image(int width, int height)`
- destructor
- copy constructor, copy assignment (deep copies)
- move constructor, move assignment (both `noexcept`; the moved-from image has width 0, height 0 and a null pixel pointer)
- `int width() const`, `int height() const`
- `unsigned char& at(int x, int y)` and a const version (the pixel at column x, row y lives at index `y * width + x`)
- `const unsigned char* pixels() const`
hints: Write them in order and test after each: constructor and destructor, then the two copies (deep), then the two moves (steal and leave the source empty).
Use one helper to allocate and copy `width * height` bytes, so both copy operations share it. Mark the move operations `noexcept`.
